exposure: Skin cytokine levels (CCL27, CXCL2, hBD-1, IL-18, IL-8, IL-1a, IL-1RA, IL-1b, S100A8/9, IL-36g)
outcome: Development of atopic dermatitis (AD) in the first year of life
Presence of AD at ages 6 or 12 months
Persistence of AD between ages 6 and 12 months
Development of AD with emollient intervention
cohort: Subsets of high-risk infants with a parent with allergic disease who participated in a randomized controlled trial.
finding: Higher titers of S100A8/9 in skin swabs from the antecubital fossa at age 8 weeks in infants with the filaggrin wild-type genotype were predictive of AD development in the first year of life and AD persistence.
